heroHeadline: MiniMax Files for Mainland China IPO as AI Capital Supercycle Deepens — Revenue Doubles, $135B+ AI Unicorn Wave Accelerates Independent of US Market Access
heroSubtitle: May 30–31, 2026 — MiniMax Group filed for a mainland China IPO on May 30 (Bloomberg), months after its January 2026 Hong Kong IPO, as the company's annualized revenue more than doubled to $300M+ and a new flagship model launch approaches. The dual-listing strategy mirrors Baidu Kunlunxin's approach and signals the maturation of China's AI capital market: the combined valuation of China's AI unicorn wave has reached ~$135B+ (DeepSeek ~$50B, MiniMax $40B+, Moonshot AI $20B, Kunlunxin $14.6B, Zhipu AI ~$14B), entirely funded by domestic capital — Alibaba, Tencent, Meituan, and China Big Fund III — without US market access or foreign capital involvement. The MiniMax mainland filing closes a landmark two-week cycle that began with DeepSeek's ~$50B Big Fund funding round and AGI declaration (May 22), the SMIC-SMNC $6B foundry consolidation (May 22-23), DeepSeek's permanent 75% V4 Pro price cut (May 26), the Qualcomm-ByteDance ASIC deal (May 26), China's AI talent travel restriction extension to private firms (May 26), the Huawei Tau Scaling Law global analyst consensus as 'Another DeepSeek Moment' (May 27), Bloomberg's yuan appreciation analysis driven by $500M/hour AI exports (May 28), Al Jazeera's 60 GW data center energy advantage report (May 28), and Bloomberg's definitive 3-year chip gap assessment between Huawei and TSMC (May 29). The TrendForce-confirmed SMIC and Hua Hong wafer price increases (May 22) confirm that domestic AI infrastructure buildout is straining Chinese foundry capacity — a signal that domestic AI compute demand is now tightening supply at both the model and hardware layers simultaneously. The structural picture that emerges across May 2026: China's AI ecosystem is now multi-vector, self-financing, and on several dimensions (energy infrastructure, model efficiency, domestic capital formation, talent retention) structurally beyond the reach of the existing US export control toolkit.
